newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's prehistoric trees up for sale.
newsitem.headline: Australia's prehistoric trees up for sale.

text.p: An Australian state government on Wednesday offered gardeners and investors the chance to buy a piece of pre-history when it announced plans to sell seedlings from a tree species which existed 150 million years ago.

The decision to put up for sale seedlings from the pre-historic Wollemi Pine trees was made in an attempt to save the species from extinction, New South Wales state environment minister Pam Allan said in a statement.
Thirty-nine of the previously unknown trees were found west of Sydney in 1994. "There is currently only a single stand of trees in one remote location in the wild," Allan said.

"Having seedlings distributed to botanical and private gardens will ensure a healthy population. It is possible that, within two or three years, Wollemi Pine seedlings will be available to Australian gardeners," she said.
Horticulturalists from the Mount Annan Botanic Garden in New South Wales had already grown 500 plants from cuttings and seeds taken from the original stand discovered in 1994, Allan said.

The government has called for expressions of interest in the international rights for commercial propagation of the trees, which existed in the time of the dinosaurs. A number of international and Australian forestry bodies had already shown an interest in growing the species for softwood plantation timber, Allan said.
"There has been a great deal of international scientific and commercial interest in the Wollemi Pine," she said.
"The awarding of a tender may...give the right to propagate and market the tree to the public, while also generating funds to preserve the species."
The trees, some measuring 40 metres (131 feet) tall and three metres (10 feet) in diameter, were found in a deep gorge 200 km (125 miles) west of Sydney.
They were described at the time of their discovery as "living fossils" and their exact location has been kept a closely-guarded secret.

While the trees can be identified as pines, or conifers, their closest relatives are extinct plants only found in fossils from the Jurassic and Cretaceous periods about 65 million to 200 million years ago.

The original stand of trees, covered in dense, waxy foliage with distinctive bubbly bark, occupy a tiny 5,000 square metre (5,980 square yard) grove of prehistoric rainforest in the 500,000-hectare (1.23 million-acre) Wollemi National Park.
